chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Ayyub ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whatever from the hadith does not accord with the Quran is mere decoration (zukhruf).

key_terms.الحديث: hadith — prophetic or imamic narrations; the body of traditions attributed to the Prophet and Imams
key_terms.القرآن: the Quran — the divine scripture, here established as the ultimate standard for authenticating hadith
key_terms.زخرف: zukhruf — literally 'ornament' or 'decoration'; figuratively, something outwardly attractive but inwardly false or fabricated; gold embellishment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about hadith that contradicts the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the Quran as the supreme criterion for evaluating hadith. Any narration that contradicts the Quran is to be rejected as zukhruf — a term that originally meant elaborate ornamentation or gilded falsehood, implying that such hadiths are attractive on the surface but fundamentally hollow or counterfeit. This principle was declared in the context of Shia hadith methodology, directing scholars and believers to test all traditions against Quranic guidance rather than accepting them uncritically.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Ayoub Bin Rashid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Whatever from the Hadeeth is not in accordance with the Quran, so it is a décor’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqba from Ayyub ibn Rashid from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“Of Hadith whatever does not agree with the holy Quran is a useless statement.”
